'''Sergio Michel''' "'''Checo'''" '''Pérez Mendoza''' ({{IPA|es-419|ˈseɾxjo ˈpeɾes|lang|SergioPérezPronunciation.ogg}}; born 26 January 1990) is a Mexican [[racing driver]] who competes in [[Formula One]] for [[Cadillac in Formula One|Cadillac]]. Pérez was runner-up in the [[Formula One World Drivers' Championship]] in {{F1|2023}} with [[Red Bull Racing|Red Bull]], and has won {{Numbertoword|{{F1stat|PER|wins}}}} [[Formula One Grands Prix|Grands Prix]] across 15 seasons.

Born and raised in [[Guadalajara]], Pérez began competitive [[kart racing]] aged six. Graduating to [[junior formulae]] in 2004, Pérez won his first championship in the national class of the [[2007 British Formula 3 International Series]]. He progressed to the [[GP2 Series]] in [[2009 GP2 Series|2009]], finishing runner-up to [[Pastor Maldonado]] the [[2010 GP2 Series|following season]] with [[Addax Team|Addax]]. A member of the [[Ferrari Driver Academy]] from 2010 to 2012, Pérez signed for [[Sauber]] in {{F1|2011}} to partner [[Kamui Kobayashi]], making his Formula One debut at the {{F1GP|2011|Australian}}, where both were disqualified for an illegal [[Downforce|rear wing]]. Pérez found greater success for the team in {{F1|2012}}, achieving his maiden podium finish in [[2012 Malaysian Grand Prix|Malaysia]], and repeating this feat in [[2012 Canadian Grand Prix|Canada]] and [[2012 Italian Grand Prix|Italy]]. For the {{F1|2013}} season, Pérez moved to [[McLaren]], replacing [[Lewis Hamilton]] to partner [[Jenson Button]]. After a podium-less season for McLaren, Pérez signed with [[Force India]] in {{F1|2014}}. He scored five podiums with the team before their re-branding to [[Racing Point]] mid-way through the {{F1|2018}} season. 

Pérez placed fourth in the championship with Racing Point in {{F1|2020}}, taking his maiden [[List of Formula One Grand Prix winners|win]] at the {{F1GP|2020|Sakhir}}, having been in last-place at the end of the first lap. Replaced by [[Sebastian Vettel]] at the re-branded [[Aston Martin in Formula One|Aston Martin]] for {{F1|2021}}, Pérez signed for [[Red Bull Racing|Red Bull]] to partner [[Max Verstappen]]; he took his first victory for the team at the {{F1GP|2021|Azerbaijan}}. Pérez took further wins in {{F1|2022}} at the [[2022 Monaco Grand Prix|Monaco]] and [[2022 Singapore Grand Prix|Singapore]] Grands Prix, amongst his maiden [[List of Formula One polesitters|pole position]] in [[2022 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix|Saudi Arabia]], finishing the season third overall. Pérez finished runner-up to Verstappen in the [[2023 Formula One World Championship|2023 World Drivers' Championship]], after additional victories in [[2023 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix|Saudi Arabia]] and [[2023 Azerbaijan Grand Prix|Azerbaijan]]. Following a winless {{F1|2024}} campaign, Pérez and Red Bull mutually agreed to terminate his contract, having contributed to two [[World Constructors' Championship]]s. He returned with [[Cadillac in Formula One|Cadillac]] in {{F1|2026}}.

Pérez has achieved {{Numbertoword|{{F1stat|PER|wins}}}} race wins, {{Numbertoword|{{F1stat|PER|poles}}}} pole positions, {{F1stat|PER|fastestlaps}} fastest laps and {{F1stat|PER|podiums}} podiums in Formula One. He holds the [[List of Formula One driver records|Formula One records]] for the [[List of Formula One driver records#Most races before first win|most starts before a race win]] (190) and the [[List of Formula One driver records#Most races before first pole position|most races before a pole position]] (219). Pérez is contracted to remain at Cadillac until at least the end of the 2027 season.

== Early and personal life ==
Sergio Michel Pérez Mendoza was born on 26 January 1990 in [[Guadalajara]], [[Jalisco]].<ref name="Sergio Perez Profile">{{cite web|date=28 January 2021|title=ESPN/How Sergio Perez rode his lifelong sponsorship to Formula One success|url=https://www.espn.com/racing/f1/story/_/id/30791634/how-sergio-perez-rode-lifelong-sponsorship-formula-one-success|access-date=24 October 2021|website=ESPN|archive-date=24 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211124205547/https://www.espn.com/racing/f1/story/_/id/30791634/how-sergio-perez-rode-lifelong-sponsorship-formula-one-success|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=McLaren Racing - Heritage - Sergio Pérez|url=https://www.mclaren.com/racing/heritage/driver/sergio-perez/|access-date=4 December 2020|website=mclaren|archive-date=4 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201204165527/https://www.mclaren.com/racing/heritage/driver/sergio-perez/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Pérez is the youngest child of Antonio Pérez Garibay and Marilú Mendoza de Pérez; he also has an older sister Paola and an older brother [[Antonio Pérez (racing driver)|Antonio]],<ref>{{cite news| url = http://www.sergioperezf1.com/| title = Bienvenidodosa PerezRacing.com| publisher = Official Pérez Brothers| access-date = 14 October 2010| archive-date = 24 January 2011| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110124004415/http://sergioperezf1.com/| url-status = live}}</ref> a retired [[stock car racing]] driver who competed in the [[NASCAR Mexico Series]]. Pérez is married to Carola Martínez Galindo, and they have four children: two sons and two daughters.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://us.as.com/us/2020/12/07/tikitakas/1607304930_653966.html|title=Así es el estilo de vida de Carola Martínez Galindo, esposa de Checo Pérez|language=es|first=Daniela|last=Barrera|date=6 December 2020|access-date=1 January 2021|work=Diario As|archive-date=25 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201225024721/https://us.as.com/us/2020/12/07/tikitakas/1607304930_653966.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Social stint: Perez father of baby son Emilio |url=https://www.gpblog.com/en/news/110699/social-stint-perez-father-of-baby-son-emilio.html |access-date=16 May 2022 |website=gpblog |archive-date=15 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220515195749/https://www.gpblog.com/en/news/110699/social-stint-perez-father-of-baby-son-emilio.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Pérez is [[Roman Catholic|Catholic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://f1i.com/magazine/30987-sergio-perez-on-a-mexican-wave.html|title=F1: Sergio Perez - On a Mexican wave|last=Silbermann|first=Eric|date=28 October 2015|website=F1i.com|access-date=3 April 2020|archive-date=20 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210220171610/https://f1i.com/magazine/30987-sergio-perez-on-a-mexican-wave.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Both Pérez brothers are association football fans, stating that they thought about leaving car racing to play professionally.<ref name=Bolavip>[https://bolavip.com/en/sports/fomula-1-how-did-sergio-perez-almost-become-soccer-player-20210328-0004.html Formula 1: How did Sergio Perez almost become a soccer player?] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413223319/https://bolavip.com/en/sports/fomula-1-how-did-sergio-perez-almost-become-soccer-player-20210328-0004.html |date=13 April 2021 }} https://bolavip.com/en {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210415224903/https://bolavip.com/en |date=15 April 2021 }}</ref> The brothers are friends of Mexican footballer [[Javier Hernández]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/motorsport/formulaone/9588516/Sergio-Perez-aims-to-emulate-his-friend-Manchester-Uniteds-Javier-Hernandez-and-win-title-for-McLaren.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/motorsport/formulaone/9588516/Sergio-Perez-aims-to-emulate-his-friend-Manchester-Uniteds-Javier-Hernandez-and-win-title-for-McLaren.html |archive-date=11 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Sergio Perez aims to emulate his friend, Manchester United's Javier Hernandez, and win title for McLaren|first=Tom|last=Cary|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=4 October 2012|access-date=29 March 2013|location=London}}{{cbignore}}</ref> In an interview in 2012 for the official Formula One website, Pérez revealed that if he had not been a driver he would have liked to have been a lawyer.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.formula1.com/news/interviews/2012/9/13787.html|title=The Inside Line – on Sauber's Sergio Perez|publisher=Formula One|date=11 September 2012|access-date=23 November 2012|archive-date=16 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121116011037/http://www.formula1.com/news/interviews/2012/9/13787.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Junior racing career ==
{{more sources section |date=March 2025}}
===Karting===
Pérez began his career in karting at the age of six in 1996.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://escuderiatelmex.com/index.php?option=com_k2&view=item&layout=item&id=27&Itemid=58&lang=en |title=Sergio Pérez Mendoza |work=Escuderia Telmex|publisher=[[Telmex]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130126104048/http://escuderiatelmex.com/index.php?option=com_k2&view=item&layout=item&id=27&Itemid=58&lang=en |archive-date=26 January 2013 |access-date=12 January 2016}}</ref> In his first year of competition he achieved four victories in the junior category and claimed the runner-up spot in the category. In 1997, he participated in the karting Youth Class, where he was the youngest driver in the category and earned a win and five podium finishes and finished fourth in the championship.

The following year, Pérez returned to compete in the junior category; he achieved eight wins and became the youngest driver to become champion of the category. He also participated in several races in Shifter 125cc and competed in Master Kadets, where he finished on the podium.

In 1999, Pérez raced in the 80cc Shifter category, taking three wins and finishing third in the championship. He also became the youngest driver to win a competition in the category, after obtaining special permission from the Federation to participate in the 80cc Shifter.

In 2000, Pérez raced in the Shifter 80cc Championship and also participated in three races in the Shifter 125cc category, which was part of the Telmex Challenge. The following year saw him become the youngest driver to compete in the 125cc Shifter Regional category. By now, his achievements were bringing him to the attention of scouts for [[Escuderia Telmex]].

With six wins in 2002, Pérez finished as the national runner-up in the Shifter 125cc category, and participated in the global race Shifter 80cc, in [[Las Vegas]], where he qualified fifth and finished in 11th place.

In 2003, Pérez was leading both championships in the 125cc category but withdrew from the last seven races, which proved to be a disappointment in his title aspirations. However, he finished in third place in Telmex Challenge, in addition to being Cup runner-up in Mexico. In the same year, he was also invited to attend the Easy Kart 125 Shootout, where he competed against drivers from around the world and won the race, again as the youngest driver.

===Skip Barber===
Pérez competed in the US-based [[Skip Barber]] National Championship in 2004. Driving for a team sponsored by Mexican telecommunications company [[Telmex]], he finished eleventh in the championship.

===Formula BMW===
Pérez moved to Europe in 2005 to compete in the German [[Formula BMW]] ADAC series. He was allowed to live in a restaurant owned by his team manager for four months.<ref name=perezmclarenbio>{{cite web|title=Sergio Pérez :: Biography|url=http://www.mclaren.com/formula1/page/sergio-p%C3%A9rez--biography|publisher=McLaren|date=4 January 2013|access-date=8 January 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130108112242/http://www.mclaren.com/formula1/page/sergio-p%C3%A9rez--biography|archive-date=8 January 2013}}</ref> He finished fourteenth in the championship, driving for 4speed Media, and improved to sixth position the following year.

===A1 Grand Prix===
In the [[2006–07 A1 Grand Prix season]], Pérez took part in a single round of the championship for [[A1 Team Mexico]]. He was the [[List of A1 Grand Prix records|third-youngest]] driver to take part in the series.

===Formula Three===
Pérez switched to the [[British Formula 3 Championship]] for [[2007 British Formula 3 season|2007]]. Pérez relocated his residence to [[Oxford]].<ref name=perezmclarenbio /> He competed in the National Class – for older chassis – with the T-Sport team, winning the championship by a comfortable margin. In the process, he won two-thirds of the races and a similar proportion of [[pole position]]s, and finished all but two races on the podium.

For [[2008 British Formula 3 season|2008]], Pérez and T-Sport graduated to the premier International Class of the championship, where he was one of the few drivers to be equipped with a [[Mugen Motorsports|Mugen Honda]] engine. After leading the championship early in the season, he eventually finished fourth in the drivers' standings.

===GP2 Series===
[[File:Sergio_Perez,_GP2_Asia_0809.jpg|thumb|right|Pérez driving for [[Campos Grand Prix]] in the [[2008–09 GP2 Asia Series]]]]
Pérez drove for the [[Campos Grand Prix]] team in the [[2008–09 GP2 Asia Series]], partnering Russian driver [[Vitaly Petrov]]. He was the first Mexican driver to compete at this level of motorsport since Giovanni Aloi took part in [[International Formula 3000]] in [[1990 International Formula 3000 season|1990]]. He won his first [[GP2 Asia Series]] race at [[Bahrain International Circuit|Sakhir]], winning from lights-to-flag in the sprint race having started from [[pole position]]. He added a second win at [[Losail International Circuit|Losail]], during the sprint race of the night meeting in [[Qatar]].

Pérez moved to [[Arden International]] for the main [[2009 GP2 Series]], driving alongside fellow [[Formula Three]] graduate [[Edoardo Mortara]]. Pérez finished twelfth in the standings, with a best result of second coming at [[Valencia Street Circuit|Valencia]]. In the off-season, he contested two rounds of the [[2009–10 GP2 Asia Series]] for [[Addax Team|Barwa Addax]], ahead of a [[2010 GP2 Series|2010 main series campaign]] with the team.<ref>{{cite news|title=Perez rejoins Addax for 2010|work=Autosport|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/80497|first=Matt|last=Beer|date=9 December 2009|access-date=13 March 2010|archive-date=5 January 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100105172127/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/80497|url-status=live}}</ref> He won five races, and finished second in the standings behind [[Pastor Maldonado]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Perez thunders to GP2 win in Abu Dhabi|url=http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/13112010/58/perez-thunders-gp2-win-abu-dhabi.html|publisher=Yahoo! Sport (Yahoo!)|date=13 November 2010|access-date=12 November 2012|archive-date=16 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130416053740/http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/13112010/58/perez-thunders-gp2-win-abu-dhabi.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Formula One career==
===Sauber (2011–2012)===
====2011: Debut season====

On 4 October 2010, [[Sauber]] announced that Pérez would join the team in {{F1|2011}}, replacing [[Nick Heidfeld]]. Sauber subsequently announced a partnership with Pérez's sponsor [[Telmex]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/87193|title=Sauber signs Perez for 2011 season|first=Pablo|last=Elizalde|work=[[Autosport]]|date=4 October 2010|access-date=1 December 2012|archive-date=23 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160923054919/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/87193|url-status=live}}</ref> He became the fifth Mexican to compete in Formula One, and the first since [[Héctor Rebaque]] competed between 1977 and 1981. He also became a member of the [[Ferrari Driver Academy]] scheme in October 2010.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/87251|title=Perez joins Ferrari young driver scheme|first=Jonathan|last=Noble|work=[[Autosport]]|date=8 October 2010|access-date=1 December 2012|archive-date=10 October 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101010072945/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/87251|url-status=live}}</ref>

Pérez finished seventh in his first race, the {{F1 GP|2011|Australian}}, impressing observers by stopping to change tyres only once, becoming the only driver in the field to make fewer than two stops.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/motorsport/formula_one/9437589.stm|first=Sarah|last=Holt|title=Sebastian Vettel beats Lewis Hamilton in Australian GP|work=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|date=27 March 2011|access-date=27 March 2011|archive-date=5 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120305115414/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/motorsport/formula_one/9437589.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> However, both Sauber cars were subsequently disqualified for infringing technical regulations.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sauber disqualified after Sergio Perez impresses|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/motorsport/formula_one/9437693.stm|work=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|date=27 March 2011|access-date=10 April 2011|first=Richard|last=Rae|archive-date=16 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190916005240/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/motorsport/formula_one/9437693.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> He failed to repeat the result in [[2011 Malaysian Grand Prix|Malaysia]] where body parts flew off [[Sébastien Buemi]]'s [[Scuderia Toro Rosso|Toro Rosso]] car and into the electrical system of Pérez's Sauber, forcing his retirement. The {{F1 GP|2011|Chinese}} saw him start in 12th position and he struggled during the race as well as making contact with several drivers en route to 17th. He followed that up with fourteenth in [[2011 Turkish Grand Prix|Turkey]], before a ninth-place finish in [[2011 Spanish Grand Prix|Spain]] – ahead of teammate [[Kamui Kobayashi]] in tenth – to take his first Formula One points.

During the third part of qualifying for the {{F1 GP|2011|Monaco}}, Pérez lost control of his car upon exiting the circuit's tunnel section, swung to the right and crashed into the barrier, before sliding across the chicane and hitting the TecPro barrier with a heavy side impact.<ref>{{cite news|title=Perez not seriously hurt in Monaco GP crash|date=28 May 2011|access-date=28 May 2011|work=[[USA Today]]|publisher=David Hunke; [[Gannett Company]]|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/motor/2011-05-28-3008638151_x.htm|first=Jerome|last=Pugmire|archive-date=31 May 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110531143059/http://www.usatoday.com/sports/motor/2011-05-28-3008638151_x.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> He was seen holding his hands around his head in an attempt to protect it just before the final impact. The session was suspended, and marshals and medical personnel extricated Pérez from his car. A Sauber team spokesman said that he was conscious and able to talk after the accident, and had been taken to the circuit's medical centre.<ref>{{cite news|last=Elizalde|first=Pablo|title=Perez conscious, talking after crash|work=Autosport|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/91795|date=28 May 2011|access-date=28 May 2011|archive-date=23 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160923054606/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/91795|url-status=live}}</ref> He suffered a sprained thigh and concussion, and did not take part in the race the following day, on medical grounds.<ref>{{cite news|last=Elizalde|first=Pablo|title=Perez ruled out of Monaco GP|work=Autosport|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/91821|date=28 May 2011|access-date=28 May 2011|archive-date=23 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160923053643/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/91821|url-status=live}}</ref> After taking part in the first practice session of the {{F1 GP|2011|Canadian}}, Pérez did not feel well enough and decided not to take any further part, and was replaced by [[Pedro de la Rosa]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/13734813|work=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|date=10 June 2011|access-date=10 June 2011|title=Sergio Perez to miss rest of Canadian Grand Prix|first=Andrew|last=Benson|archive-date=22 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190822080544/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/13734813|url-status=live}}</ref>

Pérez returned for the {{F1 GP|2011|European}} and finished eleventh after attempting to run the race on a one-stop strategy. He took a career-best seventh at the {{F1 GP|2011|British}} and eleventh in [[2011 German Grand Prix|Germany]]. After a fifteenth place in [[2011 Hungarian Grand Prix|Hungary]], he retired in [[2011 Belgian Grand Prix|Belgium]] with suspension failure. This was followed by a gearbox failure while running seventh in [[2011 Italian Grand Prix|Italy]], before he scored a point in [[2011 Singapore Grand Prix|Singapore]] after losing ninth place to [[Felipe Massa]]. In [[2011 Japanese Grand Prix|Japan]] he took eighth place, before a sixteenth-place finish in [[2011 Korean Grand Prix|Korea]], tenth in [[2011 Indian Grand Prix|India]], and an eleventh-place finish in [[2011 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix|Abu Dhabi]]. He finished sixteenth in the Drivers' Championship with fourteen points.

On 28 July, it was announced that Pérez would remain with Sauber into the {{F1|2012}} season, alongside teammate Kobayashi.<ref>{{cite news|last=Collantine|first=Keith|date=28 July 2011|title=Kobayashi and Perez to stay at Sauber in 2012|publisher=Racefans|url=https://www.racefans.net/2011/07/28/sauber-retain-kobayashi-perez-2012/|access-date=7 October 2021|archive-date=31 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220531100240/https://www.racefans.net/2011/07/28/sauber-retain-kobayashi-perez-2012/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 13 September, Pérez tested for Ferrari as part of the Ferrari Driver Academy in a [[Ferrari F60]], Ferrari's car from the {{F1|2009}} season. Pérez conducted the test with fellow academy member [[Jules Bianchi]].<ref>{{cite news|title=The Ferrari Driver Academy according to Perez and Bianchi|url=http://www.ferrari.com/English/Formula1/News/Headlines/Pages/110915_FDA_The-Ferrari-Driver-Academy-according-to-Perez-and-Bianchi.aspx|work=[[Scuderia Ferrari]]|publisher=[[Ferrari]]|access-date=4 October 2011|date=15 September 2011|archive-date=24 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110924010348/http://www.ferrari.com/English/Formula1/News/Headlines/Pages/110915_FDA_The-Ferrari-Driver-Academy-according-to-Perez-and-Bianchi.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2012: Maiden podiums====
[[File:Fernando Alonso and Sergio Perez 2012 Malaysia.jpg|thumb|right|Pérez chasing Alonso for the lead of the [[2012 Malaysian Grand Prix]], where he achieved his first podium in Formula One]]
Pérez started the season with eighth place at the {{F1 GP|2012|Australian}}, losing several places on the final lap due to excessively-worn tyres.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sauberf1team.com/en/news.cfm?id=D7S09505-Australian_GP_%E2%80%93_Race|title=Australian GP: Race|date=18 March 2012|access-date=18 April 2012|work=Sauber F1 Team|publisher=[[Sauber]] F1|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121216130521/http://www.sauberf1team.com/en/news.cfm?id=D7S09505-Australian_GP_–_Race|archive-date=16 December 2012}}</ref> In the second round at [[2012 Malaysian Grand Prix|Malaysia]], he went on to battle with [[Fernando Alonso]] for the win. [[File:Sergio Perez Canada 2012.jpg|thumb|left|Pérez on his way to third place in the [[2012 Canadian Grand Prix]], his second podium finish]]
In the {{F1 GP|2012|European}}, Pérez qualified in fifteenth place, citing a handling imbalance and the car feeling "unpredictable" as reasons for the gap to Kobayashi in seventh.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/100633|title=Europe Saturday quotes: Sauber|work=[[Autosport]]|date=23 June 2012|access-date=1 December 2012|quote=For me the car's balance wasn't good in qualifying, and the car felt a bit unpredictable.|archive-date=23 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160923051318/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/100633|url-status=live}}</ref> He improved to ninth place in the race, but raised poor qualifying form as an issue for the team.<ref>{{cite news|last=Elizalde|first=Pablo|title=Sergio Perez laments Sauber's poor qualifying form in Valencia|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/100696|publisher=Autosport (Haymarket Publications)|date=24 June 2012|access-date=12 November 2012|archive-date=27 June 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120627141357/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/100696|url-status=live}}</ref> On lap 12 of the {{F1 GP|2012|British}}, he collided with [[Pastor Maldonado]], forcing him to retire with broken suspension. He later criticised Maldonado, claiming "Everybody has concerns about him" before adding, "He is a driver who doesn't know that we are risking our lives and has no respect at all".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/101062|title=Angry Perez tells FIA to act on Maldonado after British Grand Prix accident|first1=Jonathan|last1=Noble|first2=Sam|last2=Tremayne|work=[[Autosport]]|date=8 July 2012|access-date=1 December 2012|archive-date=22 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161022021026/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/101062|url-status=live}}</ref> Maldonado received a double penalty in the form of a reprimand and a €10,000 fine after the race. Pérez later added: "Just look at the last races. He ruined [[Lewis Hamilton|[Lewis] Hamilton]]'s race (in Valencia), he ruined my race in Monaco by doing stupid things. I don't understand why the stewards don't take a serious decision with him. With Pastor they're not doing anything that will teach him a lesson."<ref>{{cite web|last=Migoni|first=Luis|title=Double Penalty for Maldonado after Peréz crash|url=http://www.fia.com/en-GB/mediacentre/f1_media/articles/britain/Pages/sunday-4.aspx|publisher=Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile|access-date=8 July 2012|archive-date=11 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120711122742/http://www.fia.com/en-GB/mediacentre/f1_media/articles/britain/Pages/sunday-4.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[File:Sergio Pérez, United States Grand Prix, Austin 2012.jpg|thumb|left|Pérez at the [[2012 United States Grand Prix]]]]
For the {{F1 GP|2012|German}}, Pérez started in 17th position but was able to make his way through the field, and ultimately finished the race in 6th place.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/18944949|title=Fernando Alonso wins tense race at Hockenheim|first=Andrew|last=Benson|date=22 July 2012|access-date=1 December 2012|work=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|archive-date=6 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106023601/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/formula1/18944949|url-status=live}}</ref> At the {{F1 GP|2012|Belgian}}, he made it into Q3 and qualified fifth fastest. A penalty for Maldonado subsequently promoted Pérez to a career-best fourth on the grid.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.crash.net/f1/news/183456/1/perez_not_too_happy_despite_personal_best.html|title=Perez 'not too happy' despite personal best|work=Crash.net|date=1 September 2012|access-date=1 December 2012|archive-date=3 September 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120903005233/http://www.crash.net/f1/news/183456/1/perez_not_too_happy_despite_personal_best.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the race, he was forced to retire in the first turn of the first lap after [[Romain Grosjean]] caused a spectacular accident. Grosjean crashed his car into Lewis Hamilton creating a domino effect which involved five cars. Also involved in the accident were, the championship leader [[Fernando Alonso]] and Pérez's teammate [[Kamui Kobayashi]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Race – Button wins after first-corner carnage in Spa|url=http://www.formula1.com/news/headlines/2012/9/13739.html|website=Formula1|date=2 September 2012|access-date=12 November 2012|archive-date=3 September 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120903233719/http://www.formula1.com/news/headlines/2012/9/13739.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Pérez took his third podium at the {{F1 GP|2012|Italian}}. On Saturday, he failed to qualify for Q3 and was twelfth on the grid. On Sunday, he climbed through the field to second place, passing on track, among others, [[Kimi Räikkönen]], [[Nico Rosberg]], [[Felipe Massa]] and Alonso. Unlike most of the drivers in the field, Pérez started the race on hard tyres and changed to the medium tyres on lap 29,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.formula1.com/news/headlines/2012/9/13780.html|title=Hamilton supreme at Monza, as Perez shines again|publisher=Formula One|date=9 September 2012|access-date=1 December 2012|archive-date=11 September 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120911004654/http://www.formula1.com/news/headlines/2012/9/13780.html|url-status=live}}</ref> allowing him to lead the Grand Prix for five laps. As a result, Pérez and his car's outstanding tyre management got him well into the points, and ultimately, to a podium finish. Ultimately, he finished the season in tenth place in the Drivers' Championship with 66 points, 6 more than teammate Kobayashi.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sauberf1team.com/en/news.cfm?id=93AQA924-Brazilian_GP_Race|title=Brazilian GP: Race|date=25 November 2012|access-date=1 December 2012|work=Sauber F1 Team|publisher=[[Sauber F1]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130104192921/http://www.sauberf1team.com/en/news.cfm?id=93AQA924-Brazilian_GP_Race|archive-date=4 January 2013}}</ref>

With his success at Sauber, Pérez was referred to as "The Mexican [[Wunderkind]]".<ref>{{cite web|last=ZumMallen|first=Ryan|title=Motorsports Monday: Hamilton On Top In Hungary, Spa 24, NASCAR At Indy|url=http://www.automedia.com/Blog/post/Motorsports-Monday-Hamilton-On-Top-In-Hungary-Spa-24-NASCAR-At-Indy.aspx|publisher=autoMedia.com|access-date=23 September 2012|archive-date=1 August 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120801073328/http://www.automedia.com/Blog/post/Motorsports-Monday-Hamilton-On-Top-In-Hungary-Spa-24-NASCAR-At-Indy.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===McLaren (2013)===
[[File:McLaren MP4-28 Perez Barcelona Test 2 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Pérez in the [[McLaren MP4-28|MP4-28]] during winter tests at [[Circuito de Jerez|Jerez]], in 2013]]
On 28 September 2012, [[Lewis Hamilton]]'s decision to leave [[McLaren]] for [[Mercedes-Benz in Formula One|Mercedes]] in 2013 was announced, and Pérez was subsequently confirmed as Hamilton's replacement.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/102891|title=Sergio Perez gets Lewis Hamilton's McLaren seat|first=Jonathan|last=Noble|work=[[Autosport]]|date=28 September 2012|access-date=1 December 2012|archive-date=14 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121114223659/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/102891|url-status=live}}</ref> He also replaced Hamilton in McLaren's cartoon ''[[Tooned]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://skiddmark.com/2012/09/exclusive-checo-perez-joins-button-for-a-new-series-of-tooned/|title=Checo Pérez joins Button for a new series of 'Tooned'..|first=Steve|last=Davies|date=28 September 2012|access-date=1 December 2012|work=Skiddmark|publisher=Fitch Media Limited|archive-date=10 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160910022404/http://skiddmark.com/2012/09/exclusive-checo-perez-joins-button-for-a-new-series-of-tooned/|url-status=live}}</ref> This also ended Pérez' association with [[Scuderia Ferrari|Ferrari]], as he was released from its driver academy.

In the season-opening race in [[2013 Australian Grand Prix|Australia]], Pérez qualified 15th and finished in 11th position, later describing the weekend as "difficult" for himself and the team as a whole.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/mclaren/motorsport/story/103587.html|title=McLaren learning from Melbourne – Perez|work=ESPN F1|publisher=ESPN Emea Ltd.|date=20 March 2013|access-date=29 March 2013|archive-date=30 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230630165649/http://en.espn.co.uk/mclaren/motorsport/story/103587.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He started the {{F1 GP|2013|Malaysian}} from ninth on the grid, and finished the race in the same position, scoring his first points for McLaren. He also achieved the fastest lap of the race, having pitted for fresh tyres.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.racer.com/vettel-beats-webber-in-malaysia-amid-team-controversy/article/285831/|title=Vettel beats Webber in Malaysia amid team controversy|work=[[Racer (magazine)|Racer]]|date=24 March 2013|access-date=29 March 2013|archive-date=29 May 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130529181303/http://www.racer.com/vettel-beats-webber-in-malaysia-amid-team-controversy/article/285831/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mclaren.com/formula1/2013/Malaysia-Grand-Prix/malaysian-grand-prix-race-report/|title=Malaysian Grand Prix Race Report|work=[[McLaren]]|publisher=[[McLaren Group]]|date=24 March 2013|access-date=29 March 2013|archive-date=23 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160923054341/http://www.mclaren.com/formula1/2013/Malaysia-Grand-Prix/malaysian-grand-prix-race-report/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In the [[2013 Bahrain Grand Prix|Bahrain Grand Prix]], Pérez started 12th on the grid and finished 6th ahead of [[Scuderia Ferrari|Ferrari]]'s [[Fernando Alonso]] (eighth) and his teammate [[Jenson Button]] (tenth), with whom he had a fierce duel in which they touched on a couple of occasions, increasing the competition between drivers in McLaren on the following races.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.formula1.com/results/season/2013/896/7209/|title=2013 FORMULA 1 GULF AIR BAHRAIN GRAND PRIX – Race Results|publisher=Formula One|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140708204303/http://www.formula1.com/results/season/2013/896/7209/ |archive-date=8 July 2014|access-date=12 January 2016}}</ref>

After the Bahrain Grand Prix, Jenson Button said of Pérez's driving style:

{{blockquote|I've raced with many team-mates over the years and with quite an aggressive team-mate in [[Lewis Hamilton|Lewis]], but I'm not used to driving down the straight and then my team-mate coming along and wiggling his wheels at me and banging wheels with me at 300km/h. I've had some tough fights in F1 but not quite as dirty as that.

That's something you do in karting and normally you grow out of it but that's obviously not the case with Checo [Pérez]. Soon something serious will happen so he has to calm down. He's extremely quick and he did a great job today but some of it is unnecessary and an issue when you are doing those speeds.|[[Jenson Button]] speaking to [[ESPN]] about Pérez after the 2013 Bahrain Grand Prix<ref name="ButtonOnPerez">{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/bahrain/motorsport/story/106407.htm|title='Dirty' driver Perez has to calm down – Button|publisher=ESPN|date=21 April 2013|access-date=1 December 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203000116/http://www.espn.co.uk/bahrain/motorsport/story/106407.htm|archive-date=3 December 2013|df=dmy-all}}</ref>}}
[[File:Sergio Perez 2013 Malaysia FP1.jpg|thumb|left|Pérez at the [[2013 Malaysian Grand Prix]]]]
At the [[2013 Monaco Grand Prix]], Pérez performed several aggressive overtaking moves, before retiring after colliding with Kimi Räikkönen. Following the incident Räikkönen said that Pérez should be "punched in the face".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/22675026|title=Monaco GP: Sergio Perez should be punched, says Kimi Raikkonen|work=BBC Sport|access-date=12 January 2016|archive-date=28 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150428124626/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/formula1/22675026|url-status=live}}</ref> Pérez recorded a season-best fifth-place finish in [[2013 Indian Grand Prix|India]], finishing four seconds shy of the podium, a result that left him "extremely satisfied".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.formula1.com/news/headlines/2013/10/15163.html|title=India – selected team and driver quotes|publisher=Formula One|date=27 October 2013|access-date=29 October 2013|archive-date=13 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220613225440/https://www.formula1.com/en/latest.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Pérez confirmed on 13 November 2013 that he would be leaving McLaren at the end of the season to be replaced by [[Kevin Magnussen]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/24927323 |title=Sergio Perez confirms McLaren departure |work=BBC Sport |date=13 November 2013 |access-date=15 November 2013 |archive-date=15 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131115035237/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/formula1/24927323 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Force India / Racing Point (2014–2020)===
====2014====
[[File:Sergio Pérez Bahrain 2014.jpg|thumb|Pérez at the [[2014 Bahrain Grand Prix]] where he achieved his first podium finish since the {{F1|2012}} season, with third place in the race]]
On 12 December 2013, exactly one month after it was announced he would leave McLaren, [[Force India]] confirmed that Pérez would join [[Nico Hülkenberg]] in their driver line-up for {{F1|2014}} in a 15 million Euro deal.<ref name="Perez joins Hulkenberg">{{cite news|title=Perez joins Hulkenberg at Force India for 2014 F1 season|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/111835|work=Autosport|date=12 December 2013|access-date=12 December 2013|archive-date=31 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170331183854/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/111835|url-status=live}}</ref>

In the {{F1 GP|2014|Australian}}, Pérez finished 11th but was moved up to tenth to get his first point for Force India due to [[Daniel Ricciardo]] being disqualified for breaching fuel limits. He failed to start the {{F1 GP|2014|Malaysian}}, after his car encountered gearbox issues before the start of the race. Nevertheless, a week later in the {{F1 GP|2014|Bahrain}}, he was able to score Force India's first podium since {{F1|2009}},<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/26916142|title=Sergio Perez and Force India revel in podium|work=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|date=6 April 2014|access-date=6 April 2014|archive-date=15 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150915145309/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/formula1/26916142|url-status=live}}</ref> holding off Ricciardo's [[Red Bull Racing|Red Bull]] for a third-place finish.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/113320|title=Perez podium 'special' after tough 2013|first1=Jonathan|last1=Noble|first2=Glenn|last2=Freeman|work=[[Autosport]]|date=6 April 2014|access-date=6 April 2014|archive-date=7 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407082259/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/113320|url-status=live}}</ref> At the {{F1 GP|2014|Chinese}}, Pérez started 16th and after gaining four places at the start, was able to overtake both McLarens and [[Daniil Kvyat]]'s Toro Rosso to finish ninth. Out-qualifying his teammate for a second time, Pérez started in the tenth position for the {{F1 GP|2014|Monaco}}. However, a first-lap collision with [[Jenson Button]] meant an early retirement for the first time in the season. At the {{F1 GP|2014|Canadian}}, Pérez was again fighting for another podium finish until the car suffered braking issues, later resulting in losing the third-place position to both Red Bulls. On the last lap, he was involved in a collision with [[Felipe Massa]], who crashed into the back of his Force India sending both cars heavily into the barriers. Pérez was subsequently given a five-place grid penalty for the next race, as the stewards decided he changed his racing line, causing Massa to crash into him.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.formula1.com/news/headlines/2014/6/15935.html |title=Pérez, Chilton penalised for Montreal collisions |date=8 June 2014 |work=ESPN F1 |access-date=8 June 2014 |archive-date=10 June 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140610021209/http://www.formula1.com/news/headlines/2014/6/15935.html |url-status=live }}</ref> At the {{F1 GP|2014|Austrian}}, Pérez set his third fastest lap of his career whilst also giving Force India their third fastest lap in their history.

On 7 November 2014, before the {{F1 GP|2014|Brazilian}}, Force India announced that Pérez would remain with the team for the {{F1|2015}} season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/formula1/29964035|title=Sergio Perez: Force India driver to stay with Formula 1 team in 2015|date=7 November 2014|access-date=7 December 2014|work=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|archive-date=24 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924230852/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/formula1/29964035|url-status=live}}</ref> Pérez stated that contract negotiations were "ongoing", in regards to a further contract extension. The deal was officially confirmed at the {{F1 GP|2014|Abu Dhabi}}, with Pérez signing a new two-year contract, until the end of the {{F1|2016}} season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/30165050|title=Sergio Perez: Force India driver signs up for 2016 season|date=22 November 2014|access-date=7 December 2014|work=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|archive-date=22 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151022184127/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/formula1/30165050|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2015====
[[File:Sergio Perez 070615.jpg|thumb|Pérez at the [[2015 Canadian Grand Prix]]]]
The 2015 season started with a tenth place for Pérez in [[2015 Australian Grand Prix|Australia]], followed by a 13th in [[2015 Malaysian Grand Prix|Malaysia]], an 11th in [[2015 Chinese Grand Prix|China]] and an eighth in [[2015 Bahrain Grand Prix|Bahrain]]. He came fifth in [[2015 Belgian Grand Prix|Belgium]] and sixth in [[2015 Italian Grand Prix|Italy]]. His best race of the season was in [[2015 Russian Grand Prix|Russia]], where he scored his first podium of 2015 and Force India's third-ever.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.escuderiatelmex.com/wps/portal/et/en/noticias/detalle/podio-gp-rusia-perez|title=Podium for Checo in Russia, fifth in his F1 history|work=Escuderia Telmex|publisher=[[Telmex]]|access-date=12 January 2016|archive-date=5 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305080716/http://www.escuderiatelmex.com/wps/portal/et/en/noticias/detalle/podio-gp-rusia-perez|url-status=live}}</ref> At the [[2015 Hungarian Grand Prix]] during the first practice session he suffered a rear suspension failure and lost control of his car which led to a barrel roll that destroyed his car, he was able to walk away from the accident unscathed.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2015/jul/24/sergio-perez-crash-hungarian-grand-prix-formula-one | title=Sergio Pérez walks away unscathed after high-speed F1 crash at Hungarian GP | website=[[TheGuardian.com]] | date=24 July 2015 | access-date=24 May 2022 | archive-date=24 May 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220524091845/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2015/jul/24/sergio-perez-crash-hungarian-grand-prix-formula-one | url-status=live }}</ref> He finished the 2015 championship in ninth, his highest championship position to date, with 78 points. He outscored teammate Hülkenberg by 20 points. Besides the podium finish in Russia, he managed three further top-five finishes in Belgium, the [[2015 United States Grand Prix|US]], and [[2015 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix|Abu Dhabi]]; he scored 63 of his 78 points in the final nine rounds. In the second half of the season, he out-qualified his teammate in six of the last nine races and eight times throughout the season.

====2016====
[[File:Pérez Monaco 2016.jpg|thumb|left|Pérez finished third in the [[2016 Monaco Grand Prix]].]]
Pérez experienced a difficult start to the season for the first four races due to an uncompetitive [[Force India VJM09|VJM09]], but scored points with a ninth-place in [[2016 Russian Grand Prix|Russia]]. Upgrades were introduced in [[2016 Spanish Grand Prix|Barcelona]] with a seventh-place finish indicating an improvement in the team's form.

In [[2016 Monaco Grand Prix|Monaco]], Pérez scored his sixth (and Force India's fourth) podium finish in wet and changing conditions and moved to ninth in the Drivers' Championship standings. Tyre management played a significant role but in contrast to previous occasions he pitted as many times as [[Scuderia Ferrari|Ferrari]] and [[Red Bull Racing|Red Bull]], at times catching up with the front runners and managing to hold [[Sebastian Vettel]] in fourth at a comfortable distance.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/f1/news/24215/10298642/sergio-perez-delighted-to-show-his-talent-with-p3-at-monaco-gp|title=Sergio Perez delighted to show his talent with P3 at Monaco GP|last=Morlidge|first=Matt|publisher=Sky Sports|date=13 June 2016|access-date=25 June 2016|archive-date=3 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220603131255/https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/24215/10298642/sergio-perez-delighted-to-show-his-talent-with-p3-at-monaco-gp|url-status=live}}</ref>

In the [[2016 European Grand Prix|European Grand Prix]] in [[Baku Street Circuit|Baku]], Pérez once again finished third, recovering from a gearbox change penalty as a result of a crash during free practice, having been fast enough to qualify on the front row. Despite having to start from seventh on the grid, he made his way up to fourth before passing Kimi Räikkönen on the last lap of the race for third, making it his second podium in three races.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/sergio-perez-picked-a-second-podium-finish-of-the-season-at-baku-790084/?tp%5B0%5D=6&s=1|title=Sergio Perez picked a second podium finish of the season at Baku|work=motorsport.com|date=19 June 2016 |access-date=25 June 2016|archive-date=15 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170115022821/http://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/sergio-perez-picked-a-second-podium-finish-of-the-season-at-baku-790084/?tp%5B0%5D=6&s=1|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/perez-hails-incredible-year-after-second-podium-790064/?s=1|title=Perez hails "incredible" year after second podium|work=motorsport.com|date=19 June 2016 |access-date=25 June 2016|archive-date=15 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170115022204/http://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/perez-hails-incredible-year-after-second-podium-790064/?s=1|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2017====
[[File:2017 British Grand Prix (35548214990).jpg|thumb|right|Pérez at the [[2017 British Grand Prix]]]]
After the [[2016 Malaysian Grand Prix]], Pérez confirmed he had committed to Force India for the 2017 season. He remained with the Indian team for a fourth consecutive season alongside new teammate [[Esteban Ocon]], ending speculation of a possible move to [[Williams Grand Prix Engineering|Williams]], [[Renault in Formula One|Renault]] or [[Haas F1 Team|Haas]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/126441/perez-commits-to-force-india-for-2017|title=Sergio Perez commits to Force India for 2017 F1 season|first=Ian|last=Parkes|work=Autosport|access-date=3 October 2016|archive-date=2 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161002024426/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/126441/perez-commits-to-force-india-for-2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.formula1.com/en/latest/headlines/2016/10/perez-to-stay-at-force-india-in-2017.html|title=Perez to stay at Force India in 2017|publisher=Formula One|access-date=3 October 2016|archive-date=26 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210726223418/https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/headlines/2016/10/perez-to-stay-at-force-india-in-2017.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He was very consistent with his highest finish in 2017 a fourth place in [[2017 Spanish Grand Prix|Spain]] after two rivals collided at the start, and a third retired mid-race with a power unit failure.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://en.f1i.com/news/268160-perez-targets-red-bull-after-taking-fourth-in-barcelona.html|title=Perez targets Red Bull after taking fourth in Barcelona|work=en.f1i.com|date=14 May 2017|access-date=14 May 2017|archive-date=10 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810051115/http://en.f1i.com/news/268160-perez-targets-red-bull-after-taking-fourth-in-barcelona.html|url-status=live |last1=Lewin |first1=Andrew }}</ref> He ended his streak of 17 points finishes as he ended up colliding with Daniil Kvyat in [[2017 Monaco Grand Prix|Monaco]]. He had a moment with his teammate in [[2017 Canadian Grand Prix|Canada]] when he did not allow his teammate through, who thought he could challenge Daniel Ricciardo for third. He was again knocked out in [[2017 Azerbaijan Grand Prix|Baku]] where he thought he could challenge for the win before colliding with Ocon. He finished seventh in [[2017 Austrian Grand Prix|Austria]] and moved up to sixth in the standings after [[Max Verstappen]] was out of the race on the first lap. He dropped to seventh in the championship after finishing ninth in [[2017 British Grand Prix|Britain]], behind his teammate and Verstappen finished fourth. He remained seventh in the standings for the rest of the season.

====2018====
[[File:FIA F1 Austria 2018 Nr. 11 Perez.jpg|alt=|thumb|Pérez at the [[2018 Austrian Grand Prix]]|left]]
Pérez finished the first three races of the season outside the points. He then achieved his eighth career podium finish at the [[2018 Azerbaijan Grand Prix|Azerbaijan Grand Prix]], finishing third after an incident-strewn race. He passed then-championship leader [[Sebastian Vettel]] for third place with a few laps to go, making him the first driver to finish on the podium twice at the [[Baku City Circuit]] (in [[2016 European Grand Prix|2016]] and [[2018 Azerbaijan Grand Prix|2018]]). Another points finish came with ninth place in [[2018 Spanish Grand Prix|Spain]]. In [[2018 French Grand Prix|France]], he retired from the race with an engine failure. Three consecutive points finishes followed, with seventh-place finishes in [[2018 Austrian Grand Prix|Austria]] and [[2018 German Grand Prix|Germany]].

[[File:Ilham Aliyev watched the opening ceremony of the 2018 Formula-1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix and final race 32.jpg|thumb|The podium ceremony at the [[2018 Azerbaijan Grand Prix]]: [[Lewis Hamilton]], [[Kimi Räikkönen]] and Pérez]]

After the [[2018 Hungarian Grand Prix|Hungarian Grand Prix]], Force India was put into [[Administration (law)|administration]]. This was caused by a group of creditors (including Pérez) taking legal action against the team. Pérez said that this action was taken to save the team and its employees from a winding-up order instigated by other creditors, which would have resulted in the team's collapse.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://speedcafe.com/perez-explains-force-indias-financial-position/|title=Perez explains Force India's financial position|website=speedcafe.com|date=29 July 2018|access-date=5 January 2020|archive-date=29 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180729081416/https://www.speedcafe.com/2018/07/29/perez-explains-force-indias-financial-position/|url-status=live}}</ref> Shortly before the [[2018 Belgian Grand Prix|Belgian Grand Prix]], Force India's assets were purchased by a consortium of investors led by [[Lawrence Stroll]], father of [[Williams Grand Prix Engineering|Williams]] driver [[Lance Stroll]]. The team was re-admitted into the championship as a new team—[[Racing Point Force India]]—keeping Pérez and Ocon as their drivers. At the Belgian Grand Prix, the team came back strong with Pérez and Ocon qualifying fourth and third, and finishing fifth and sixth, respectively.

Pérez took seven points finishes from nine races in the second half of the season. However, he faced criticism after a poor performance in [[2019 Singapore Grand Prix|Singapore]]. He collided with his teammate Ocon on the opening lap, causing Ocon to crash into a wall and retire from the race. He also collided with [[Sergey Sirotkin (racing driver)|Sergey Sirotkin]], an action that resulted in a drive-through penalty. He later stated that he thought his penalty was "fair".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/138761/perez-admits-sirotkin-clash-penalty-fair|title=Sergio Perez admits penalty for Sergey Sirotkin clash was 'fair'|website=Autosport|date=16 September 2018|access-date=5 January 2020|archive-date=11 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201111223904/https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/138761/perez-admits-sirotkin-clash-penalty-fair|url-status=live}}</ref> He later suffered a brake failure and retired from his home race in [[2018 Mexican Grand Prix|Mexico]]. He ended the season in eighth place in the championship with 62 points, finishing ahead of teammate Ocon and being the only non-Mercedes, Ferrari or Red Bull driver to finish on the podium that season.

Pérez won his first race at the [[2020 Sakhir Grand Prix|Sakhir Grand Prix]], becoming Formula 1's 110th race winner. On the first lap, Pérez was hit by Leclerc and went from 2nd place to 18th and last. On lap 64 he took the lead and won the race ahead of [[Esteban Ocon]] and teammate Stroll. This was the first win for a Mexican driver since [[Pedro Rodríguez (racing driver)|Pedro Rodríguez]] won the [[1970 Belgian Grand Prix]] 50 years prior.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.sergio-perez-takes-sensational-maiden-win-in-sakhir-gp-as-tyre-issues-ruin.2TBf7rg5wpgELNALXJLRHV.html|title=Sergio Perez takes sensational maiden win in Sakhir GP as tyre mix-up ruins Russell's charge|date=6 December 2020|website=formula1|access-date=9 December 2020|archive-date=7 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201207063434/https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.sergio-perez-takes-sensational-maiden-win-in-sakhir-gp-as-tyre-issues-ruin.2TBf7rg5wpgELNALXJLRHV.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.statsf1.com/en/2020/sakhir/tour-par-tour.aspx|title=Sakhir 2020 - Lap by lap|website=www.statsf1.com|access-date=4 January 2021|archive-date=9 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210109120941/https://www.statsf1.com/en/2020/sakhir/tour-par-tour.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref>
